candidate.answerReason: A circle of radius a passes through the fixed point exactly when its center is distance a from that point.

methods.label: Translate the condition into a distance
methods.explanation:
Let \(P\) be the fixed point, and let the given radius be \(a>0\). If a circle with center \(C\) and radius \(a\) passes through \(P\), then \(CP=a\).

Conversely, whenever \(CP=a\), the circle centered at \(C\) with radius \(a\) passes through \(P\). Thus the possible centers are exactly the points at distance \(a\) from \(P\). These points form a circle centered at \(P\) with radius \(a\), so the answer is \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
methods.levelReason: The argument uses only the defining fixed-distance property of a circle and proves both directions of the locus description.

candidate.annotationRationale: The target is recognizing a circle from its center-radius distance condition. The method uses the same condition both to restrict possible centers and to show every point on the proposed locus is allowed. Point-to-point distance is supporting knowledge.

review.mathematicalCheck: For the positive radius \(a\), an eligible center \(C\) satisfies \(CP=a\), and every such point produces an eligible circle. This proves that the locus is exactly the circle centered at \(P\) with radius \(a\).
review.levelCheck: The elementary circle definition is sufficient, and both directions are clearly established.
